note: Skeptic Shark, operator angle. Fresh-context only — judged against the four numbered North Star surfaces, not the codebase. Heartbeat written at `planning/chatgpt-terminal-2026-09-05/stage1/artifacts/heartbeat.json`.

findings.section: Phase 4 — live Playwright sign-off and v1.2.12 ship gate
findings.criterion: 4 — a ChatGPT terminal is opened from the dashboard and its greet is seen on the page (Playwright screenshot), not inferred from a stub
findings.message: The only operator proof is skippable (`ANCHOR_TESTS_ALLOW_LIVE=1`) and the ship rule is "the screenshot file exists." No greet string is named. A blank xterm, a Codex login wall, an approval modal, or a copied PNG all satisfy "file exists." Criterion 4 is a claim about John's page, not about a path on disk. As written, v1.2.12 can ship with the greet still inferred.

findings.topic: live sign-off on unseeded general lane
findings.section: Phase 4 — live sign-off test / Phase 2 seed timing
findings.criterion: 1 — the lane seed is written exactly once and the greet arrives
findings.message: The dashboard action the live test clicks is "Open terminal," which is a bare `general` session — historically no lane skill. Playwright then waits for unnamed "Codex greet text" and records `seed_delivery`, which is not the skill loading. Criterion 1 is a seeded trio cockpit, not a chrome banner. An operator who then starts Research/Plan/Build on ChatGPT is running the unproven path. Phase 2's stub done-when (`seeded True`) and Phase 4's live button do not even agree on which lane is the proof.

findings.topic: picker hardcodes ready without binary probe
findings.criterion: 2 — picker shows "ChatGPT — ready"; a host without the Codex binary still fails closed; risk table — picker shows "unavailable" there
findings.message: Phase 1 sets `selectable=True`, `status='ready'`, and a static reason "Codex CLI detected…" with no detection. Tests pin "no seat is disabled." On a host without `codex`, the operator is told the seat is ready and detected, then `term_start` dies with `chatgpt-terminal-binary-missing`. The North Star already chose the operator-visible mitigation — the picker says unavailable — and this draft implements the opposite lie.

findings.section: Phase 1 done-when vs Phase 2 launch argv
findings.criterion: 2 — the Terminal picker shows "ChatGPT — ready" AND 1 — PTY running the Codex TUI with `--cd`, `--no-alt-screen`, `-s workspace-write`
findings.message: Phase 1's definition of done is the picker and capability note saying ready, while the launch is still bare `codex` (alt-screen, no `--cd`, no sandbox). That is the operator-visible surface going green before the terminal can actually open as specified. Any mid-effort restart, or a saved `default_cli=chatgpt` after wave 1, presents a first-class seat that hits the exact alt-screen failure the risk table named. "Ready" is a surface claim, not a permission to open a gate.

findings.section: Phase 2 — seed timing / switch_engine relaunch sites
findings.criterion: 1 — `POST /api/rnd/term_set_engine` switches a live session to and from ChatGPT; the lane seed is written exactly once and the greet arrives
findings.message: First-output-gated seed is specified for `start_session`. Engine switch is the operator's other way onto ChatGPT (criterion 1 names it). The draft applies launch argv at both relaunch sites but does not apply `SEED_AFTER_FIRST_OUTPUT_BACKENDS` there. Toggling Claude → ChatGPT can dump the skill into a composer that is not up — the seed-before-ready risk, on the hotter operator path. Phase 4 asserts no orphan PTY after toggle, not that the ChatGPT side was seeded after first output.

findings.criterion: 1 — approvals left to the user in the terminal; risk table — seed must not land before the TUI is ready, nor as an approval
findings.message: On timeout the plan still writes the seed ("never leave a live session silently unseeded"). That is how a login wall or on-request approval becomes the seed's target — the operator's first keystrokes answer Codex, or the skill is submitted as the approval. The draft also refuses to inject `-a` and treats "no flag" as "on-request," which is an assumption about v0.151 defaults, not a pin. Criterion 1's approval contract is therefore unenforced on the path most likely to fire on a real open.

findings.criterion: 3 — session usage state is `uncorrelated`; any rollup that includes it is stamped `partial (chatgpt segment unmeasured)` — never an mtime guess, never a fabricated $0.00
findings.message: The draft asserts three stamps at once: empty `stored_engine_uuid` → W4 `uncorrelated`; `usage_unmeasured_segments` + `classify_session_usage` "measured + any segment → STATE_PARTIAL"; and "ended on chatgpt with no reason is stamped chatgpt-segment." The operator-facing badge is then whichever branch wins. Criterion 3 split session vs rollup on purpose. As written, a ChatGPT session can show as partial, or a rollup can inherit a session-level reason, and the "no $0.00 / never mtime" test does not say which widget John reads.

The function is stub-tested. The done-when then names "the Doctor Diagnose button with backend chatgpt" without saying how that button chooses ChatGPT — default_cli, a picker, or a hidden argument. John does not call `live_doctor_session`. If Diagnose stays on Claude (or on write-posture default_cli), the read-only Codex Doctor never appears on the surface criterion 3 is for. A stub argv walk is not Doctor-capable in the cockpit.
